links.outcome: User agreement, confidence, and verification behavior under output-, relation-, and token-level uncertainty displays
links.effect: Token-level uncertainty increased agreement with the AI; output- and relation-level did not increase agreement but reduced users' confidence in own answers; relation-level also reduced external verification.
links.quote: Token-level uncertainty increased users' agreement with the AI, whereas output- and relation-level uncertainty did not increase agreement but instead reduced users' confidence in their own answers.

links.outcome: Effect of displayed uncertainty at different granularities on user reliance and verification
links.effect: Relation-level uncertainty reduced external verification (internet searches, checking URLs), steering users toward reliance on the LLM and its uncertainty cues; token-level increased agreement.
links.quote: Notably, relation-level uncertainty also reduced external verification (i.e., internet searches, checking provided URLs), steering users away from independent fact-checking and toward reliance on the LLM and its accompanying uncertainty cues.

links.outcome: Whether uncertainty display design promotes user verification of LLM outputs
links.effect: Uncertainty granularity shaped verification: relation-level reduced external verification, token-level increased agreement, output-level reduced self-confidence without more agreement.
links.quote: Our findings demonstrate that uncertainty granularity significantly shapes how users interact with and verify LLM outputs, providing concrete design guidance for building responsible LLM applications that encourage appropriate skepticism and verification behaviors.
